signatures.description: Given a directory of Bitcask-style append-only data files (record = crc32c, timestamp, key size, value size, key, value) plus a possibly stale hint file, rebuild the in-memory keydir by replaying the log, honoring tombstones and monotonic file-id/offset write ordering, and treating a checksum mismatch or short read at the tail of the newest file as a torn append to truncate rather than as fatal corruption. Implement offline merge/compaction that rewrites only live keys in monotonic order, emits a fresh hint file, and fully reclaims space for dead keys, while a mid-file (non-tail) corruption must exit 3 and print the exact byte offset of the first bad record. Ship tests proving every key reads back its last-committed value after recovery and that a second compaction run is a byte-level no-op.
